source_fields.question_text: Let <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math> be a polynomial of degree <math><mn>5</mn></math> such that <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>n</mi><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> for <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><mn>3</mn></math>, <math><mn>4</mn></math>, <math><mn>5</mn></math>, <math><mn>6</mn></math>, <math><mn>7</mn></math>. Find <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
source_fields.explanation: Define <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>. Then <math><mi>q</mi></math> has degree <math><mn>7</mn></math> and zeros at <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> to <math><mn>7</mn></math>, so <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>29</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>27</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>⋯</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mn>40320</mn></math> using the conditions <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Evaluating gives <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>37</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></math>, so <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>8</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>56</mn></mfrac></math>.

derived_fields.sub_skill: Using auxiliary polynomials and root-factorization to determine coefficients
derived_fields.problem_family: Find the value of a polynomial at a new point given its values at several integers by constructing an auxiliary polynomial with prescribed roots
solve_strategy: Introduce q(x) = (x^2 - 1) p(x) - x so that q(n)=0 for the given integer inputs n because (n^2-1)p(n)-n = 0.
Recognize deg q = deg p + 2, so q is degree 7 and thus equals (ax + b) * P(x), where P(x) = ∏_{k=2}^7 (x - k).
Use evaluations at x=1 and x=-1 to produce two linear equations for a and b (these points annihilate the (x^2-1) factor so q(±1) give small integers).
Solve the 2×2 linear system for a and b, compute P(8) and evaluate q(8) = (a*8 + b)*P(8).
Recover p(8) from p(8) = (q(8) + 8)/(8^2 - 1) and reduce the resulting fraction.
derived_fields.reasoning_pattern: Transform the problem by multiplying by a factor that cancels the denominator at known inputs to create a polynomial with known integer roots, then determine its missing linear factor via evaluations at special points.
logic_invariants: For each given integer n in {2,3,4,5,6,7}, q(n) = (n^2 - 1)p(n) - n = 0.
q(x) is divisible by P(x) = ∏_{k=2}^7 (x - k); therefore q(x) = (ax + b)P(x).
Evaluations at x = 1 and x = -1 eliminate the (x^2 - 1) factor so q(±1) equal -1 and +1 respectively, giving linear constraints on a and b independent of p(±1).
P(8) = 6! = 720 is used to scale q(8) and relates to factorial-like products of consecutive integers.
changeable_parameters: list_of_integer_points_where_values_known (start and length, consecutive or nonconsecutive)
value_formula_at_these_points (e.g., n/(n^2 - 1), linear in n, other rational forms)
auxiliary_factor_used (e.g., x^2 - 1 or x^2 - a) that clears denominators
target_evaluation_point (the x at which p(x) is requested)
parameter_constraints: Number of independent conditions provided must be consistent with deg p (to avoid under- or over-determined systems); with deg p = d, providing d+1 independent values determines p uniquely.

The auxiliary factor chosen should cancel denominators at the provided inputs (i.e., its zeros should match any n that make denominators zero) or be chosen so cancellations produce integer/known q(±1) values.
When representing q(x) = (ax + b)P(x), P(x) must have degree equal to the number of distinct known roots; to make q one degree higher, multiply P by a linear factor (ax + b).
Avoid selecting known input values that make denominator zero unless the construction explicitly handles the resulting indeterminate p(n).
derived_fields.answer_format: Multiple-choice letter plus numeric content as a reduced rational fraction (e.g., 3/56).
rendering_notes: Preserve MathML tags exactly when rendering: all <math>...</math> and embedded <mi>, <mo>, <mn>, <mfrac>, <msup>, etc. must be kept.

generation_knobs: vary degree_of_p; vary consecutive integer range (length and start); vary numerator/denominator form (e.g., n/(n^2 - k), an+b over polynomial); change auxiliary factor (x^2 - 1 -> x^2 - c); change target evaluation point (8 -> other integer).

safe_variations: change the consecutive integer block while adjusting degree accordingly; replace n/(n^2-1) with other rational forms that are cleared by a simple auxiliary factor; ask for p at a different integer not among provided points.

unsafe_variations: include provided n that make denominators zero without adjusting construction (introduces undefined p(n) unless handled); pick value_formula that does not lead to a polynomial p of the specified degree; choose nonconsecutive points without providing enough conditions to determine the polynomial.

novelty_opportunities: use auxiliary factors of higher degree (e.g., (x^2 - a)(x - b)) to craft problems with multi-parameter linear factors; ask for coefficients of p rather than a single value; ask for p at a point inside the given set to test handling of removable singularities.

validation_rules: ensure the number of provided constraints matches degree+1 (or explicitly state additional structure to make the polynomial unique); verify that auxiliary factor zeros and provided input set are consistent; check arithmetic simplifications (factorials and cancellations) and fraction reduction.
risk_flags: Misinterpreting p(1) or p(-1): although p(±1) may be undefined because denominator zero, q(±1) are still well-defined and provide constraints.
Arithmetic errors in computing large products like P(1) or P(-1) (factorials) and sign mistakes when evaluating products of negatives.
For generated variants, accidentally producing an underdetermined or overdetermined system if the relationship between degree and number of points is not preserved.
Failing to reduce rational answers to lowest terms or mismatching the multiple-choice letter with the computed numeric value.
